theme_portfolio_projects.title: Order & Inventory Platform
theme_portfolio_projects.description: Stock control for a three-branch retailer, replacing a shared spreadsheet that was the single point of failure. Every sale decrements stock inside a transaction, and a low-stock threshold is what drives reordering — not a weekly report someone had to remember to run.

theme_portfolio_projects.title: Clinic Booking & Records
theme_portfolio_projects.description: Appointment scheduling, patient history and printable prescription PDFs for a two-doctor practice. The scheduling screen is built around the one question that actually matters — who is free in this half-hour — so double-booking is impossible rather than merely discouraged.

theme_portfolio_projects.title: Headless Storefront on a Laravel API
theme_portfolio_projects.description: A Next.js catalog and cart in front of a Laravel REST API, with token auth and the order pipeline kept server-side. Moving the storefront off the theme was what let the same catalogue data serve the site, a POS and a marketplace feed without three copies of the truth.

theme_portfolio_projects.title: WooCommerce Store Rescue
theme_portfolio_projects.description: A slow, plugin-heavy store brought back to a usable load time by object caching, query cleanup and a rebuilt checkout — with the order history migrated across intact. The brief was a performance problem; the thing that actually unlocked the fix was tracing where the slow requests were coming from rather than guessing at plugins.

theme_portfolio_hero_tagline: I design and build Laravel applications that stay maintainable as they grow: clean architecture, versioned REST APIs, Livewire admin panels, queues and payments, shipped with tests and CI.
theme_portfolio_availability: Open to Laravel projects and full-time roles

theme_portfolio_experiences.description: Taking Laravel applications from schema to deployment and maintaining them afterwards. Most of the week is spent on the unglamorous half of the job: reading a slow query, untangling a requirement that changed halfway through, and writing the migration that makes the next change boring.

Built the REST APIs and admin panels other teams depended on. Learned to treat a database index and a clear error message as features, because both are what a user experiences when something goes wrong at 2am.
Store builds, plugin work and migrations for small retailers — usually taking a site that had grown one plugin at a time and giving it a shape it could keep growing in.
